content.title: Another historic night by Flagg powers Mavericks past Lakers | Dallas Mavericks
content.text: If the Los Angeles Achers weren't already in a heap of pain, they certainly were after Cooper Flagg put a hurtin’ on them Sunday night.The Mavericks rode their red-hot rookie superstar to a 134-128 win over the Lakers for their first victory at American Airlines Center since Jan. 29. They stopped a 14-game home losing streak to move their record to 25-53.With no Luka Doncic and no Austin Reaves – both sitting with injuries – the Lakers fell to 50-28.And the Flagg rookie of the year train continued to roll down the tracks.Flagg followed up his 51-point outburst on Friday with a 45-point showing against the Lakers, becoming the first rookie to put up back-to-back 40-point games since Allen Iverson in 1997. He also added nine assists and eight rebounds.The 6-9 19-year-old was asked what, if any, statement was made by scoring 96 points in two games this weekend.“I think it’s definitely some sort of statement," he said, "but it goes back to what I’ve said: I’m confident in myself and know what I’m capable of and I’ll just let the rest of that stuff figure itself out."The rookie of the year race has come down to Flagg and Charlotte's Kon Knueppel, his teammate last season at Duke. Flagg having two games like this, including Sunday's on national television, certainly is providing ROY voters with lots of convincing arguments.“I don’t know if he’s making a closing statement, I think he’s just doing what he’s been doing all season," coach Jason Kidd said. "Being able to play different positions, never complained, and he’s delivered for us."And tonight, being able to do on national television 40 points is not easy, especially coming off a 50-ball. Just the way he’s playing. And he wants to win and helped the team win tonight."It was Flagg that slithered into the gut of the Lakers' defense and coaxed in a midrange jumper to get past 40 points and put the Mavericks up 126-116 with 3:26 remaining. Flagg got some help from P.J. Washington and Naji Marshall as they held on down the stretch.The ailing Lakers fell back on their tried and true safety net. LeBron James piled up 30 points, 15 assists and nine rebounds. He fell short of a triple-double, but teammate Luke Kennard did not, getting 15 points, 16 rebounds and 11 assists.But this was Flagg's night. Again. He put together a massive, 19-point first quarter and just kept going from there. At halftime, he had 26 points and James had 22. It was a wonderful back-and-forth from two superstars separated by 22 years.“It’s crazy," said Washington, who had 15 points. "To watch LeBron at 41 doing what he’s doing and obviously Coop is only 19. I think it shows how much talent we have in this league. LeBron’s one of the greatest of all time."But Coop, his future’s bright. He’s doing such great things at 19, I can’t imagine what it’s going to look like at 25. The future’s bright for us down here in Dallas."Flagg called Sunday one of the moments he will remember most about this season that has been dominated by losing streaks and injuries to numerous key players.Going up against James was a treat for fans, and Flagg, too. They guarded each other on many occasions.“I think it’s pretty cool," Flagg said. "Obviously, when I was a little kid (I was) watching him go through his whole career. It’s really impressive to watch him and see what he can still do out there. It’s a dream come true. These are the moments, to match up against somebody like that, obviously one of the greatest. It’s incredible."Kidd said that the bookends in terms of player ages in the NBA put on a show that should not be taken for granted.“The future is extremely bright," Kidd said. "But before we put LeBron to rest, he’s showing the world at the age of 41 that he can still play the game at a high level. He displayed that tonight. It just shows no matter what age, as long as you take care of your body and mind, you can do amazing things. And that’s what he’s doing."And when you talk about the youth, Cooper’s part of that group. The NBA’s in good hands as we go forward."The great matchup with Flagg and James made up for any luster this game might have lost with the absence of Doncic, who leads the league in scoring at 33.5 points per game, but was injured on Thursday with a hamstring strain. He was ruled out for the rest of the regular season and the Lakers likely will be without him early in the playoffs.Reaves, who is second on the Lakers at 23.3 points per game, is out after suffering a left oblique injury. He, too, could miss time in the playoffs.But James and Flagg made sure the energy didn’t wane.Kidd was asked about what he would like to see Flagg learn from James.“Everything,” he said. “You talk about winning. You talk about longevity. You talk about always improving their game each year. It’s not easy to be one of the best.“He’s taken care of his body, but the biggest thing is he’s taken care of his mind, making sure that that’s fresh. A lot of these kids he’s playing against were in diapers or some of them weren’t born.”Including Flagg, who was three years, two months away from being born when James made his NBA debut on Oct. 29, 2003.But he looked like the seasoned veteran in the first quarter, when he had 19 points, his best-scoring first quarter of the season.This truly was a battle of the superstars. When James stepped in front of a Flagg pass in the third quarter, it started a fast break that ended with James' thunderous dunk off a lob pass from Kennard.It was an ooh and ahh moment that put a big grin on James' face.But it was Flagg would get the final laugh.
